result.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing
result.summary: Aerial sensing must combine uncertain overhead context with current observations while budgeting prediction, movement and image processing. AeroBelief uses the next executable action as the unit of verification against reference scores. It groups candidate views by first action, scans them with an inexpensive proposer, and selectively queries a structured world model (WM). Calibrated group bounds support strict commitment; a six-query controller connects selective prediction with belief updates, acceptance checks and scheduled sensing. Across four layout families, 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, the AeroBelief controller completes 75.42% of tasks, compared with 73.33% for exhaustive WM scoring and 65.83% for line-of-sight geometry, using 91.81% fewer reference-candidate evaluations than exhaustive scoring. In fixed-reference replay with a six-query cap, proposer-scaled anchored bounds raised first-action certificate availability from 36.25% to 54.69% and reduced mean queries per state by 13.54% relative to unit-scale anchored bounds. A complete ground-hosted pipeline processes 2,685 self-collected 20-megapixel unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images from seven DJI Mavic 3M routes. Context-guided admission and feedback retain all eight independently supported target confirmations with 76.05% fewer processed images and 70.02% less accumulated active processing service than uncapped all-frame processing; feedback saves another 5.17% of images relative to static context. The studies connect budgeted action selection with evidence-driven processing of recorded flight imagery.

AI.brief_summary: AeroBelief 面向航空感知，把「下一个可执行动作」作为验证单元：先用廉价 proposer 按首个动作分组扫描候选视角，再有选择地查询结构化世界模型，并用校准的组界与六次查询预算下的控制器串联信念更新、接受检查与按需图像处理。
AI.relevance_reason: 以动作级选择性验证、校准下界和预算上限来分配证据获取，与 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本权衡及「证据充分即提交」的停止准则可能同构，其 first-action certificate 与查询预算设计可供核查。
